chunks: And from him, from Ibn Jabala, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the wealthy woman who has performed her obligatory Ḥajj, who says to her husband, 'Let me perform Ḥajj from my own wealth.' Is it for him to prevent her from that? He said, 'Yes, and he says to her, 'My right upon you is greater than your right upon me in this matter.'
And there is no harm for the woman to perform Ḥajj without a maḥram (male guardian) if she does not have a maḥram, provided she are trustworthy regarding herself. Narrated.
ai.seo_question: Does a husband have the right to prevent his wealthy wife from performing voluntary Hajj with her own money?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the hierarchy of spousal rights, establishing that a husband’s permission is required for his wife’s voluntary Ḥajj due to his superior claim on her resources and time. It further provides a practical legal exception, permitting travel without a *maḥram* if she is financially capable and secure, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on safety and trustworthiness (*amāna*) in female travel.
